newsitem.title: FINLAND: Partek disposal to finance Sisu buy - CFO.
newsitem.headline: Partek disposal to finance Sisu buy - CFO.

text.p: Finnish Partek will use the 190 million markka it will receive from the sale of a stake in Eastern Partek to help finance its merger with vehicle maker Sisu, Chief Financial Officer Kari Heinisto said.
Heinisto told Reuters on Tuesday the deal, with Singapore's NatSteel, was part of the cargo handling equipment group's increasing focus on key operations.

Since the buyer was already the majority owner of Eastern Partek, he said the sale was straightforward. Partek said earlier it would book a 90 million markka gain on the sale which Heinisto said would be paid in cash.
"We have this acquisition of Sisu in two stages," Heinisto said when asked how the funds would be used.
"The agreement has not yet been finalised so I cannot yet say when the gain will be booked," he added.

Partek announced its merger with state-owned Sisu in January. As part of the deal Partek's biggest owner Norwegian Aker swapped its Partek shares for 17 million Sisu shares which represent a 46.2 percent stake: Partek aims to buy these at 46.03 markka each, plus interest accrued.
Before interest that would total 787 million markka.
Another deal is also helping Partek to free up some of the 800 million markka that it had invested in the precast business, Heinisto said.

Asked to list Partek's remaining non-core assets, Heinisto said a new joint venture in concrete elements with Sweden's Addum and Industry Kapital aimed at broadening its ownership base has freed up a significant share of the total investment.
Partek's stake in the joint venture is 40 percent although the bulk of the business came from Partek, he said. Partek also has real estate holdings which are non-core, he added.
